question.title: Rate Limiter
question.description:
Build a rate limiter that controls how many requests are allowed in a time window.

EXAMPLE:
const limiter = new RateLimiter(3, 1000); // 3 requests per second
limiter.allowRequest(); // true
limiter.allowRequest(); // true
limiter.allowRequest(); // true
limiter.allowRequest(); // false (limit reached)
// After 1 second passes, requests are allowed again

followUpQuestions.questionText: What happens if we have millions of requests? How would you optimize memory usage?
followUpQuestions.answer:
Strong candidates should:
• Identify that storing all timestamps causes memory growth
• Propose cleanup of old timestamps
• Mention token bucket or leaky bucket algorithms
• Discuss distributed rate limiting (Redis)

Red flags:
• Doesn't recognize memory issue
• No optimization ideas

followUpQuestions.questionText: How would you handle rate limiting across multiple servers?
followUpQuestions.answer:
Look for:
• Centralized storage (Redis, Memcached)
• Distributed consensus challenges
• Trade-offs between accuracy and performance

Bonus:
• Mentions eventual consistency
• Discusses sharding strategies

followUpQuestions.questionText: What are the differences between sliding window and fixed window rate limiting?
followUpQuestions.answer:
Should explain:
• Fixed window: Simple but allows bursts at boundaries
• Sliding window: More accurate but more complex
• Trade-offs in implementation complexity vs accuracy

Strong answer:
• Explains with examples
• Discusses when to use each
